newsitem.title: UK: Safe-haven sterling exploits bout of EMU concern.
newsitem.headline: Safe-haven sterling exploits bout of EMU concern.

text.p: The pound zoomed higher against the mark on Tuesday, capitalising on concern about whether Italy, Spain and other "peripherals" will join the first wave of European monetary union (EMU), traders said.

Selling had gathered momentum in the Spanish and Italian bond markets on Monday and spilled over into the forex market after a series of statements from German officials threw the two countries' participation into question.
Sterling and the gilt market benefited from their perceived safe-haven status because it is assumed by many that Britain will not join EMU from its planned start in 1999, traders said.

"Sterling has gained from the market's renewed nervousness about EMU," said Peter Wood, forex trader at Bank of Boston in London. "The pound's good fundamentals are still in place, and there are still good reasons to buy it, which is why quite a few buyers stepped in at lower levels."

The debate about whether Italy and Spain will join the first EMU wave was fanned further by Bank of England (BOE) Governor Eddie George, who said late on Monday that it would be foolish for Europe to rush into EMU if convergence criteria are not met.
Forex traders said it was now fully priced into sterling that Finance Minister Kenneth Clarke and BOE Governor George would leave interest rates on hold at their monetary meeting on Wednesday.
"The pound is the flavour of the month once again despite a minimal chance of higher rates on Wednesday," said Jeremy Hawkins, senior economic adviser at Bank America in London.

The latest upmove comes after two weeks of sterling declines - from a 52-month high at 2.7240 on January 22 to just above 2.61 last Friday - as expectations of a rise in British interest rates receded after a spate of soft economic data.
At 1208 GMT the pound traded at 2.6645 marks, down from an earlier peak at 2.6720 but up from 2.6510 in late European trading on Monday.
Many traders still bet on a rise in rates after the British election though, which must be held by May 22, as economic growth continues at an above-trend rate.
Interest rate expectations elsewhere in Europe and in Japan continue to be focused on easier credit rather than tightening, so sterling is bound to benefit from the prospect of a British rate rise.

Fund buying of pounds for yen pushed sterling/yen to fresh highs for the move up at 198.66 yen from 193.83 at the previous European close. Sterling has also had a good run against the French franc lately, rising to 8.9960 near the European midsession from around 8.85 at the start of the week.

General sterling strength also buoyed the pound against the dollar after a dip below the psychologically important $1.60 level last Friday. At 1201 GMT it stood at $1.6230, up from $1.6125 in late European trade on Monday.

Less favourable interest rate differentials between sterling and the dollar are likely to limit the pound's upside against the U.S. currency though, analysts said. The pound is now well off its four-year peak of $1.7163, hit on December 31.
